rejected.title: Volcanic eruptions as hazards
card: A volcano is an opening in the Earth's crust where molten rock, ash and gas can escape. An eruption is when these burst out.
Lava flows
streams of molten rock that run downhill. They are slow enough that most people can walk away, but they destroy buildings, roads and farmland in their path.
Ash fall
small pieces of rock and glass thrown high into the air. Heavy ash can collapse roofs, harm crops and make it hard to breathe. It can also stop planes from flying.
Gases and hot flows
Poisonous gases such as sulfur dioxide can harm people and animals. A pyroclastic flow is a fast, hot cloud of ash and rock that rushes down a volcano's slopes and is very hard to outrun.
rejected.remember: An eruption can harm people through lava, ash, gases and hot flows. Speed matters: lava is slow, pyroclastic flows are not.

opts: A fast, hot flow of ash and rock down a volcano
A slow stream of molten rock running downhill
A cloud of fine ash that falls over distant towns
A poisonous gas that seeps out of the ground
a.why: A pyroclastic flow is a fast, hot cloud of ash and rock that rushes down the slopes. A slow stream of molten rock is a lava flow, which is the most tempting wrong answer because both are hot and move downhill.
a.clue: Think of the hazard that is both hot and very fast.

b.q: Tom farms 40 km from a volcano that has just erupted. For hours, a grey, gritty powder drifts down from the sky. His shed roof sags under the weight. Which hazard is this?
opts: Ash fall
Lava flow
Pyroclastic flow
Poisonous gas
b.why: Tiny pieces of rock and glass thrown high into the air, then drifting down and weighing on roofs, are ash fall. A pyroclastic flow also contains ash, but it rushes along the ground down the volcano's slopes rather than drifting down from the sky.
b.clue: Did it come down from above or rush along the ground?

b.q: A volcano near a town erupts. Ash is thrown high into the air and drifts over the town. Heavy ash settles on houses and farms. Which hazard is this?
opts: Ash fall, which can collapse roofs and harm crops
Lava flow, which can burn farms as it runs downhill
Pyroclastic flow, which rushes down the volcano's slopes
Poisonous gas, which can harm people who breathe it
b.why: Ash thrown into the air that settles on roofs and crops is ash fall. A pyroclastic flow is also made of ash, but it rushes along the ground down the slopes. It does not drift through the air and settle over a town.
b.clue: Which hazard falls from the sky rather than flowing along the ground?

a.best: A fast, hot flow of ash and rock down a volcano

b.best: Ash fall, which can collapse roofs and harm crops

a.q: Which of these describes a pyroclastic flow?
opts: A fast, hot flow of ash and rock down a volcano
A slow stream of molten rock running downhill
A cloud of fine ash that falls over distant towns
A poisonous gas that seeps out of the ground
a.why: A pyroclastic flow is a fast, hot cloud of ash and rock that rushes down the slopes. A slow stream of molten rock is a lava flow, which is the most tempting wrong answer because both are hot and move downhill.
a.clue: Pyro means fire, and clastic means made of broken bits of rock.

opts: Ash fall
